No changes are needed for the frontend Dockerfile. The backend Dockerfile will remain unchanged, and no MongoDB client will be added to the image. The compose file will include a MongoDB service with a volume, healthcheck, and backend dependency on the database.

MongoDB will use a simple local connection string without authentication. The MongoDB volume will be added to `.gitignore`. Documentation updates will be kept minimal, as the user requested only compose and Dockerfile changes.

A minimal application.yml will map the MONGO_URI environment variable. This ensures Spring Boot 3 will not fail if the MongoDB starter is added later. The Gradle build file will not be modified.

The MongoDB volume will be named `mongodb_data` and mapped to port 27017 for local access. The backend will depend on both Postgres and MongoDB services. Environment variables will use local demo values rather than secrets. I will check for an existing `.env.example` file.

  "plan": "# Integrate MongoDB into Compose\n\nScope is **infra wiring only**: run Mongo next to Postgres and pass a connection URI into the backend. No ticket documents, Spring Data Mongo repositories, or frontend/Nginx rewrite in this change.\n\n## Current state\n\n- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) has `postgres`, `backend`, and `frontend`. Backend waits on a healthy Postgres and gets `DB_URL` / `DB_USERNAME` / `DB_PASSWORD`.\n- [backend/Dockerfile](backend/Dockerfile) is a Java 21 multi-stage `bootJar` image with `curl` for `/actuator/health`. It does not (and should not) install a Mongo client.\n- [frontend/Dockerfile](frontend/Dockerfile) is Next.js; it never talks to the database. **Leave it unchanged.**\n- [backend/src/main/resources/application.yml](backend/src/main/resources/application.yml) only configures the JDBC datasource. Compose `MONGO_URI` would be unused until this file maps it.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  ui[frontend]\n  api[backend]\n  pg[postgres]\n  mongo[mongodb]\n  ui --\u003e api\n  api --\u003e pg\n  api --\u003e mongo\n```\n\n## Compose ([docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml))\n\nAdd a `mongodb` service in the same style as Postgres:\n\n- Image: `mongo:7` (official, includes `mongosh` for healthcheck).\n- Container name: `support_ticket_mongodb`.\n- Port: `27017:27017`.\n- Named volume `mongodb_data` → `/data/db`.\n- Database name `support_ticket` via `MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE` (no extra root user unless we keep parity with Postgres passwords; use unauthenticated local demo URI to stay simple and avoid committing a second password pair — Compose already uses `postgres/postgres` for Postgres).\n- Healthcheck: `mongosh --quiet --eval \"db.adminCommand('ping')\"` with similar interval/retries as Postgres.\n\nWire the backend:\n\n- `MONGO_URI: mongodb://mongodb:27017/support_ticket`\n- `depends_on` both `postgres` and `mongodb` with `condition: service_healthy`\n\nDo not add Redis, extra networks, or a Mongo admin UI.\n\n## Backend config (needed for the env var to mean something)\n\nUpdate [backend/src/main/resources/application.yml](backend/src/main/resources/application.yml):\n\n```yaml\nspring:\n  data:\n    mongodb:\n      uri: ${MONGO_URI:mongodb://localhost:27017/support_ticket}\n```\n\nSpring Boot ignores this until `spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb` is on the classpath. **Do not add that dependency in this pass** (no ticket persistence yet). **Scope:** git commands/rules/README/prompt-history only. No product spec, API, or app code. No secrets. No CI checks on the head commit. Mergeable: clean.

- **`/preview-merge-pr` vs constitution II.** The constitution still requires a **human** to review a PR before merge to `main`. This command lets the agent review, run tests, and merge in one go.
